climate_pressure: Exceptional extreme rainfall during Storm Daniel; anthropogenic influence is plausible but highly uncertain.
documented_impact: Flooding, dam failures, widespread physical damage, service disruption and displacement.
fcv_mediator: Infrastructure maintenance, institutional fragmentation, disaster planning, warning interpretation and coordination.
possible_consequence: Extreme rainfall can produce much larger human and economic losses where dam safety, maintenance, emergency governance and exposure are inadequate.
alternative_explanations: infrastructure quality and emergency decisions independently affected losses
uncertainty: The magnitude of anthropogenic influence on the rainfall is highly uncertain; no evidence apportions total losses quantitatively among rainfall, dams and governance.
compact_statement: Derna demonstrates compound disaster risk, not simple climate causation. (World Weather Attribution)

climate_pressure: Multiple climate hazards requiring coordinated preparation.
documented_impact: Weak/incomplete climate planning, degraded infrastructure and uneven emergency/recovery capacity.
fcv_mediator: Divided governance, institutional rivalry, weak coordination and conflict legacy.
possible_consequence: Fragmentation may reduce the maintenance, planning and coordination needed to prevent climate shocks from becoming disasters.
geographies: with strongest direct disaster evidence in eastern Libya
affected_groups: especially communities relying on fragile public infrastructure
alternative_explanations: procurement and sanctions/external constraints may also affect implementation
uncertainty: Direct evidence varies by institution; national institutional weakness does not imply identical municipal performance.
compact_statement: FCV-related institutional fragmentation is a documented constraint on climate resilience.

climate_pressure: Warming, drought, declining mean rainfall and rainfall variability.
documented_impact: Water stress, irrigation pressure and reduced rural livelihood resilience.
fcv_mediator: Water allocation, livelihood dependence, inequality, institutional legitimacy and market conditions.
possible_consequence: Where access is perceived as inequitable and livelihood alternatives are weak, worsening water stress could increase grievances or local tension, but violence is not an automatic result.
uncertainty: No strong national causal estimate links temperature or rainfall change to violent events.
compact_statement: Water scarcity becomes an FCV risk through governance and livelihoods, not through climate alone. (SIPRI)

climate_pressure: Chronic water stress potentially intensified by warming and reduced rainfall.
documented_impact: Dependence on shared, vulnerable water infrastructure.
fcv_mediator: Allocation rules, control of pumps/infrastructure, perceptions of fairness and mutual dependence.
possible_consequence: Scarcity and shared infrastructure may produce either contestation or cooperation depending on governance arrangements and incentives.
affected_groups: Communities and users dependent on shared water systems
alternative_explanations: infrastructure condition and local power relationships can drive both service interruptions and cooperation independently of climate
uncertainty: Duration and transferability of cooperative arrangements are not evaluated.
resilience_factors: credible allocation procedures and shared maintenance agreements
compact_statement: Water dependence is not intrinsically conflictual; institutions determine whether it divides or connects communities. (SIPRI)

climate_pressure: Drought, heat and other climate stressors.
documented_impact: Livelihood disruption among some migrants and climate-sensitive communities.
fcv_mediator: Conflict, income loss, migration policy, protection conditions, routes, markets and household resources.
possible_consequence: Climate shocks may contribute to decisions to move, but available Libyan evidence does not establish them as a dominant or sufficient cause of migration.
uncertainty: The 25% climate-shock figure is sample-based association, not causal attribution.
resilience_factors: service inclusion and safe mobility options
compact_statement: Climate may be one migration stressor, but Libya's mobility dynamics remain strongly multi-causal. (SIPRI)

documented_impact: Humanitarian, service and reconstruction needs after Derna.
fcv_mediator: Competing authorities, checkpoints, securitized access, institutional rivalry and social/legal status.
possible_consequence: Fragmented security governance can delay aid and make recovery less inclusive, particularly for groups with weak protection or documentation.
alternative_explanations: scale of destruction and administrative capacity also constrained response
uncertainty: Available evidence is predominantly qualitative regarding the magnitude of delay/exclusion.
resilience_factors: transparent reconstruction processes and status-neutral service provision
compact_statement: Political-security fragmentation affected who could deliver and receive recovery assistance. (SIPRI)

climate_pressure: Flooding, heat, drought and water stress.
documented_impact: WASH, health and education disruption; unreliable services.
fcv_mediator: Pre-existing public-service weakness, displacement status, poverty, documentation and gender/age-related vulnerability.
possible_consequence: Climate shocks may create larger welfare losses for people already facing weak services or barriers to assistance.
geographies: Strongest direct evidence in eastern flood zones
structural service weakness is national with regional differences
alternative_explanations: discrimination and chronic service underinvestment create vulnerability independently of climate
uncertainty: Differentiated quantitative outcome data are limited.
resilience_factors: resilient WASH/health systems and protection-sensitive disaster planning
compact_statement: Climate exposure intersects with pre-existing service and protection inequalities.

climate_pressure: Drought, heat, water scarcity and disaster risk.
documented_impact: Recognition of planning, infrastructure and technical-capacity deficits.
fcv_mediator: Institutional coordination, financing, local implementation capacity and shared-resource governance.
possible_consequence: The new drought and water strategies and local water/DRR investments could strengthen resilience and create practical cooperation incentives if implementation becomes sustained and inclusive.
alternative_explanations: Strategies may remain underfunded or fragmented
infrastructure investments may fail without maintenance and governance reform
uncertainty: Independent outcome evidence for 2025-2026 initiatives is not yet available.
compact_statement: Libya has emerging resilience assets, but implementation rather than policy adoption is the critical test. (UNDP)
